children: By Jack Pitcher and Sam Goldfarb

Following months of relative calm, stocks took a beating across the tech sector, with chip makers, upstart cloud companies and AI hyperscalers all coming under pressure. By the end of session, the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite and the S&P 500 had both logged their biggest one-day declines since July.

In an illustration of how the market is suddenly facing threats from all directions, the small-cap focused Russell 2000 also fell, dropping nearly 2%. The benchmark, which can often be more interest-rate sensitive, is now in correction territory, off more than 10% from its all-time high in August. Read more on the market tumult here.
